observation.visible_scene: Outdoor shot against a dark green horizontal-plank shed wall. A disposable aluminum foil tray sits on a stand in the lower center, with a tall orange-yellow flame rising from it and leaning to the left. At the right edge a person's arm holds a yellow garden-hose nozzle; a thin, straight water stream runs from the nozzle down-left to the tray, and a misty cone of droplets surrounds the nozzle. A brick wall and a potted plant are partly visible at the far right.
visible_changes: The flame continuously flickers and reshapes (turbulent tongues, varying brightness) while keeping roughly the same overall height and leftward lean; its base stays at the tray throughout.
The spray of droplets at the nozzle grows from a small puff in the early frames into a wider, more diffuse cone by the later frames.
The hand/nozzle shifts slightly and tilts a little downward over the segment, but the thin water stream remains directed toward the tray.
The shed wall, tray, and plant remain fixed in frame, indicating the camera is essentially static; observed motion is object motion (flame, spray, hand).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the water is intended to put out the flame and what happens after the segment (the flame is still burning at the last frame).
What material is burning in the tray and how the fire was started.
The moment the spray pattern began to widen (it is already underway at the first frame).
uncertain_details: The exact relationship between the thin jet and the misty cone at the nozzle (separate spray setting vs. atomization of the same stream) is not clear.
Small apparent shifts of the nozzle could be hand motion rather than camera motion; background evidence is insufficient to confirm any camera movement.
Slight leftward drift of the flame column over time may be flicker rather than sustained translation.
